# SEO and GEO audit: acme-mugs The repo is a small client-side-rendered React/Vite SPA with 2 routes. It has one blocking problem (the whole site is disallowed from crawling), and most of the rest comes from the app being client-rendered with no metadata. ## Critical 1. **`public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks every crawler from the whole site.** - `User-agent: *` with `Disallow: /` keeps Google, Bing and AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended) away from every page. - Fix: replace it with the following, and add AI-bot rules only if you want to treat them differently. ``` User-agent: * Allow: / Sitemap: https:///sitemap.xml ``` - If this block is deliberate because the site is still in staging, apply it only in non-production builds. 2. **`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:5-7` loads the product list only in the browser.** - `useEffect` fetches `/api/mugs` after load, so the initial HTML has an empty `

Catalogue

` and no products. - Crawlers that don't run JavaScript see nothing, and most AI crawlers don't run it. Google may render it, but later and less reliably. - Fix: pre-render or server-render the page, for example with SSR (React Router framework mode, or Next.js or Remix) or build-time static generation that fetches the data. The catalogue content must be in the HTML response. 3. **`index.html:1-11` is the only HTML shell, and every route shares it.** - `/` and `/catalogue` are served the same empty `
`. Content only appears after JavaScript runs. This is the same root cause as item 2, applied to the home page. - Fix: use the same SSR or static pre-render approach for both routes. ## High 4. **`index.html:5` has the placeholder title `Vite App`.** - Every page has the same meaningless title. - Fix: set a unique title per route, for example "Handmade Ceramic Mugs | Acme Mugs" and "Mug Catalogue | Acme Mugs". Use `` in React 19, or a head manager. 5. **`index.html:3-6` has no meta description, canonical link, `lang` attribute or viewport tag.** - Missing `<html lang>` at line 2. - Missing `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`, which hurts mobile-friendliness. - Missing `<meta name="description">` per route, and `<link rel="canonical">` per route. 6. **`src/main.jsx:11` renders the Catalogue nav item as a `<button>` with `navigate()`.** - Crawlers follow `<a href>` links, not click handlers, so `/catalogue` is not discoverable from the home page. - It is also worse for accessibility, since middle-click, open-in-new-tab and screen-reader link semantics don't work. - Fix: use `<Link to="/catalogue">Catalogue</Link>` as on line 10, and remove the unused `useNavigate`. 7. **`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11` renders products as bare `<p>` tags.** - There are no per-product pages or URLs, no links, no prices, no images and no descriptions. - Search engines and AI answer engines have nothing to index or cite for individual mugs. - Fix: add routes like `/catalogue/:slug` for each product, and link to them from the list with a real `<a href>`. Use `<ul>` and `<li>` or `<article>` markup, with name, price, image and description. ## Medium 8. **There is no structured data anywhere.** - Add JSON-LD (`Organization` and `WebSite` on the home page, `Product` with `offers`, `price`, `availability` and `image` per product, and `BreadcrumbList`). - This is the main way to be correctly understood and cited by AI search and to get rich results. 9. **`src/pages/Home.jsx:5` has `<img src="/hero.jpg" />` with no `alt`, `width` or `height`.** - A missing `alt` loses image-search value and fails accessibility checks. - Missing dimensions cause layout shift (CLS). - If this is the above-the-fold hero image, add `fetchpriority="high"` and don't lazy-load it. - Fix: `<img src="/hero.jpg" alt="Handmade ceramic mug on a wooden table" width="1200" height="800" />`. Also confirm that `hero.jpg` exists, since there is no `public/hero.jpg` in the repo. 10. **There is no `public/sitemap.xml`.** - Add one listing `/`, `/catalogue` and every product URL, and reference it from `robots.txt`. 11. **There are no Open Graph or Twitter Card tags (`index.html`).** - Without `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image` and `twitter:card`, shared links render poorly. 12. **`src/pages/Home.jsx:3-7` has very thin content.** - It is one H1 and one sentence. - AI engines cite pages that answer questions directly. Add some content (what makes the mugs different, materials, sizes, care instructions, shipping and returns, an FAQ, and who makes them), written as plain, quotable statements. - The Bristol and worldwide-shipping claims are good entity facts, so state them again in structured data. ## Low and GEO extras 13. **There is no `llms.txt` in `public/`.** This is optional and its benefit is unproven, but it is cheap. Add a short summary of the site and links to the key pages. 14. **Single-page routing needs a server fallback.** Make sure unknown URLs return a real 404 status and not `index.html` with a 200, to avoid soft-404s. This can't be seen from the repo, so check the hosting config. 15. **`package.json` has no `build` step beyond `vite build`.** There is no pre-render or sitemap generation, and `vite` is listed under `dependencies` rather than `devDependencies` (cosmetic). 16. **There is no About, Contact or shipping page and no author or business information.** These trust and E-E-A-T signals (location, maker, contact details) help both search rankings and AI citation. ## Suggested order 1. Fix `robots.txt` (item 1). 2. Move to SSR or pre-rendering (items 2 and 3). 3. Add titles, descriptions and canonicals (items 4 and 5). 4. Fix the nav link (item 6). 5. Add product pages, JSON-LD and a sitemap (items 7, 8 and 10). 6. Do the image, content and OG fixes (items 9, 11 and 12). I haven't changed any files. I can implement these if you want. Items 1, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10 are quick, and the SSR migration is the biggest change.
